# Owner-loop interaction probe: the retained records

This is the timestamped evidence behind
[the owner-loop interaction verdict](owner_loop_interaction_verdict.md). Every
number that verdict states about a stall's duration, the callbacks delivered
inside it, or the owner turns that did not happen is checkable here, against
the records the probe actually produced.

It is Markdown, and the records are inside fenced blocks, for the same reason
[the macOS confinement receipt](macos_confinement_verdict.md#the-retained-receipt)
is: a tracked non-Markdown file under `docs/` is an undeclared validation input,
and a run that added one would report an unknown input and select every
non-optional group. `*.md` is classified as prose no execution reads, so the
evidence lives beside the document that argues from it.

## What is here, and what is not

Two sessions are retained **complete**: every record the probe emitted, in
order, nothing sampled and nothing elided. Between them they carry all three
interactions #200 asked about, and every claim in the verdict rests on one of
them.

| Session | Seconds per phase | Records | `HETOIMASIA_INTERACTION_PROBE_OUTPUT` | SHA-256 of that file | What it carries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B | 20 | 39009 | `/tmp/owner-loop-interaction-trace-2.tsv` | `e20a1691eb32fc99ee9d25494468d17141d7eb07609d1c9728a148c9b3c013f7` | The move and resize measurements the verdict leads with. |
| C | 10 | 11615 | `/tmp/owner-loop-interaction-trace-3.tsv` | `76697403e4419fd9dad7fc4ef464a4462a95554ceab1b8ffd38d266eab84dbb7` | The menu-bar measurements, and a second independent move and resize. |

The SHA-256 is of the file the probe wrote, byte for byte; the fenced blocks
below are that file's contents. The paths were in `/tmp` and are gone, so the
hash is a link back to what was generated, not somewhere to fetch it.

A third, earlier session is **not** retained at record level. Its phases cannot
be attributed — the person could not see the phase banners and was pacing from
memory, so each interaction landed a phase late — and the verdict relies on
nothing from it. Its report is kept at
[the unattributable session](#the-unattributable-session) so the disclosure is
not merely an assertion.

## Reading a record

Each line is `sequence`, `offset_ms`, `event`, tab-separated. The sequence
number is issued in order from one **per session**, to kept and dropped records
alike, so consecutive numbers prove nothing was dropped between them and a gap
would name exactly how many were. The offset is milliseconds from the first
record **of that phase**, on the one monotonic clock every record in the session
shares. Each phase's header repeats its own `lost` and `faults` counts; every
one of them is zero in both retained sessions.

A stall is read directly: a `pump entered` record, then every callback the
platform delivered from inside that call, then the matching `pump left`. The
difference of the two offsets is the duration the verdict states, and the
difference of the two sequence numbers, less one, is the callback count — no
other record can appear between them, because the thread that would write one
is the thread that is blocked.

## How to check the verdict's headline numbers

In session B's `window resize` phase, find `pump entered (wait 100.000 ms)` at
offset `3575.025` and the next `pump left`, at `72493.493`. The difference is
**68 918.468 ms**. Their sequence numbers are `14557` and `37503`: `37503 −
14557 − 1 = 22 945` records between them, every one a callback, which is the
count the verdict states.

In session C's `menu-bar interaction` phase the same reading gives **13 295.111
ms** between offsets `6708.359` and `20003.470`, with two callbacks between the
two sequence numbers.

In session B's `window move` phase, no `pump left` is more than 1.105 ms past
the 100 ms its `pump entered` asked for, and `update hook entered` appears 2128
times: that is the negative result.

That nothing was dropped needs no trust in the counters either. Session B's
records run `1` to `39009` and session C's run `1` to `11615`, each contiguous
across every phase with no gap anywhere, which is what a session that lost no
record looks like from the outside.

## The unattributable session

Run before both of the above, at 20 seconds per phase, with the terminal
full-screen so the phase banners could not be seen. The interactions landed one
phase late: nothing at all during the phase labelled `window move`, a window
move during the phase labelled `window resize`, and a live resize during the
phase labelled `menu-bar interaction`. The menu bar was never reached. Its
record file was written to `/tmp/owner-loop-interaction-trace.tsv`, SHA-256
`ef272fa8e70b4840c6b3760d86475534d83b76d7adc81b2a81da323538464c1f`,
and is not retained here. Its report is:

Read it only as corroboration that a live resize blocks the pump: one
`glfwWaitEventsTimeout` of 100 ms that did not return for 29 591.851 ms, with
10 173 callbacks delivered from inside it. The phase it is reported under is
not the interaction that produced it.
